5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  OPEN SPACE AN RECREATION ELEMENT

Surabhi Barbhaya, Michael Baker International presented an overview on the topics that will be
included in the Open Space and Recreation Element and noted that the Open Space Element is
required based on the OPR guidelines and the Recreation Element is not, therefore, the two are often
combined to create one Element. Ms. Barbhaya further explained that Open Space is any undeveloped
land dedicated to open space use and provide access to nature; Recreation includes the activities that
happen within indoor or outdoor spaces. In addition, Recreation can be divided into two categories -
active and passive recreation.
Ms. Barbhaya stated that the National Recreation and Parks Association releases a report annually
which provides the average acres of park land per thousand people in communities with a population
less than 20,000; the national average is 11.8 acres per 1,000 residents1. The City of Rolling Hills
Estates is at an average of 7 acres per 1,000 residents. Neighboring communities may have higher
averages, but there may not have the same accessibility to that acreage. This City has 60% of people
living within 10 minutes walking distance to a park.
Ms. Barbhaya stated that approximately 20.5% of the City’s land area is dedicated to open space,
parks and recreation, but of that, 5% is dedicated to parks and recreation. There are 8 parks in the
City, of those there are 3 mini parks, 3 neighborhood parks, and 2 community parks. Three new parks
are being proposed in the City.

1
  As of 2017, the City provides about 56 acres of park space and 103 acres of open space, for a total of about 159
acres. With a population of approximately 8,000, the city currently has a ratio of about 7.0 park acres per 1,000
residents, well above the 1992 General Plan service standard of 4.0 acres per 1,000 residents. Using the total 159
acres of both park space and open space, the City would be providing 20 acres per 1,000 residents.

General Plan Advisory Committee  1
Meeting Minutes, December 17, 2019
 Ms. Barbhaya provided data from the Public Engagement Summary, which includes that 75% of those
surveyed believe it is important to preserve environmental resources, and 51% believe it is important
to preserve the city’s equestrian character.
COMMITTEE MEMBER SILVANO stated that she believes that many in the equestrian community
may not have completed the survey. CHAIR SCHMITZ explained the importance of the equestrian
community to participate when these opportunities arise in order for the city to be able to address their
needs or concerns.
COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA asked for clarification that the Office of Planning and Research
does not require a certain ratio of open space per residents. Ms. Barbhaya stated that is correct.
Ms. Barbhaya stated that the following, also from the Public Engagement Summary, is a list of things
that the community would like to see in parks and recreation, they include: recreation facilities, dog
parks, skate park, public pool, improved existing pedestrian and bicycle trails, expand equestrian
related trails and recreational facilities, create and improve outdoor athletic fields, community meeting
space, and expand Rolling Hills Country Club.
Ms. Barbhaya continued with a review of the existing policies. There was consensus among the GPAC
Members whether or not to move forward with the policies included in the draft General Plan Update
within the Open Space and Recreation Element.
No longer relevant, remove:
    Policy 2.3 Many of the open space and park areas are currently designated for very low
  density residential uses. They should be re-designated to reflect their actual use and to ensure
  future open space, recreational, or park use.
    Policy 2.5 Encourage the use of vacant school sites for recreational use.
Move forward with the following changes:
    Policy 1.1 Preserve natural open space areas and design future recreational facilities to
  protect the local natural environment for present and future generations.
   Policy 1.1 Preserve natural open space to protect the local natural environment for
  present and future generations.
   Policy 1.2 (new) Design future recreational facilities to respect (or protect) the local
  natural environment for present and future generations.
Move to the Housing Element for discussion:
    Policy 1.2 Maintain the rural and lower density character of Rolling Hills Estates which is
  defined by the presence of wide open spaces and low density development.
Move to the Conservation Element for discussion:
    Policy 1.3 Preserve and enhance the natural environmental and cultural heritage of the
  Peninsula and of the City of Rolling Hills Estates.
Move forward with the changes noted:
    Policy 1.4 Cooperate Coordinate with neighboring cities, local organizations, the County
  and the State in the planning for recreational and open space programs to preserve and
  enhance the Peninsula's natural environment and cultural heritage.
Covered in a previous policy, remove:
    Policy 1.5 All efforts should be made to preserve existing open space areas and other
  undeveloped land where appropriate.
Move forward:
    Policy 2.1 Promote a cooperative, neighborly and cultural community by encouraging
  recreational programs which stimulate, educate and enrich the lives of residents.
    Policy 2.6 Encourage local citizens groups to participate in the planning, development and
  maintenance of recreational facilities.
Move forward with the following changes:
    Policy 3.1 Encourage property owners to contribute lands to the City for open space and
  recreational use. One such organization involved in preserving open space in the City is the
  Pepper Tree Foundation.
  Encourage property owners to work with the Pepper Tree Foundation and other similar
  organizations and foundations to acquire and preserve land for open space and recreational
  use.

Meeting Minutes, December 17, 2019
     Policy 3.2 Seek County, State and/or Federal funds or the possibility of sharing funds with
  other agencies and organizations to acquire additional parkland or develop additional facilities.
  Seek County, State, Private and/or Federal funds or the possibility of sharing funds with other
  agencies and organizations to acquire additional parkland or develop additional facilities.
Move forward:
    Policy 3.6 As stated in the Transportation Element (Policy 3.1), encourage the development
  of connections between existing trails where feasible.
    Policy 3.7 Proposed subdivision developments, new construction, and additions should be
  reviewed for compliance with the City's trail plan, and the improvement programs outlined in
  the Open Space and Recreation Element.
Move forward with the following changes:

    Policy 3.8 The City will work with property owners, community organizations and other
  agencies so that existing multi-use trails are maintained where appropriate.

Move forward:
  •  Policy 2.2 Cooperate in sharing a Peninsula-wide system of parks and recreational facilities.

  •  Policy 2.7 Preserve and promote the equestrian and hiking trail network within the City of
  Rolling Hills Estates.

Move forward with the following change:

  •  Policy 2.8 Provide a permanent site for an Equestrian Center, similar to what now exists and
  prepare a general design and operational plan for the facility.

  Preserve and maintain the Peter Weber Equestrian Center at its current location.
This policy is similar to a policy in the Conservation Element, remove:
  •  Policy 2.9 Review and amend as appropriate ordinances relating to equestrian facilities within
  residential areas. The ordinances must take into consideration storage.

No longer relevant, remove:

  •  Policy 2.10 Identify a location for a Community Center.

Move forward with the following change:

  •  Policy 3.3 Develop Consider plans for financing the acquisition of open space areas should
  they be placed on the market by current property owners.

This has been completed, remove:

  •  Policy 3.4 Review and revise ordinances (such as the Quimby Ordinance) to require builders
  and developers to provide lands and/or funds for acquisition and development of land for
  recreational use.

Move forward with the following change:

  •  Policy 3.5 Strive to maintain or increase the current ratio of parkland to population. The current
  ratio of parkland to City residents must be maintained or increased and not be less than the
  current ratio of 6.7 acres of parkland for every 1,000 residents.
Remove:
    Increase access to parks by exploring opportunities to create new entrances or creating safe
  routes around obstacles like busy streets.
    Explore potential opportunities develop community meeting area/ senior center.
Move forward:
    Explore availability of new sites for the development of mini parks, and neighborhood parks
  especially in the underserved areas of the community.

General Plan Advisory Committee  3
Meeting Minutes, December 17, 2019
 Move forward with the following change:
    Explore opportunities to develop additional recreational amenities including playground, skate
  park, dog parks, and community gardens.
Move forward:
    Develop recreation facilities that have multi-use capabilities when possible.
    Where appropriate, co-locate park and recreation facilities with other community oriented
  spaces, such as the public library and other publicly accessible commercial areas, so that it
  may function as the “heart” of a community.
    Explore opportunities in commercial areas to create public open spaces such as plazas, pocket
  parks, and parklets that foster Placemaking.
Remove:
    Explore the feasibility to designate and develop the Palos Verdes land fill area, or portion
  thereof, for the park and recreational use.
Move forward:
    Strive to create contiguous open space and multi-use trail networks.
    Include hitching posts for horses in new parks and explore opportunities to include them in
  existing parks that are connected with existing and proposed equestrian trails.
COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN suggested that a policy be created to consider repurposing of water
to increase the quality of the parks.
Mr. Bellas stated that a new policy will be drafted to include the following:
    If reclaimed/recycled water becomes available, prioritize city parkland and city fields.

Move forward:
    Develop a parks and recreation master plan for the community to identify land, programming,
  funding, and maintenance of existing and future facilities.
    Consider equestrian access to parks and recreational areas when developing future
  transportation or mobility plans.
    Develop universal design guidelines for trails, parks, and public open spaces to increase
  accessibility to the park system.
B.  INTRODUCTION TO PUBLIC SAFETY ELEMENT
The introduction to the Public Safety Element will be presented at the next GPAC meeting.
6.  CONSULTANT/STAFF/COMMITTEE ITEMS
The GPAC discussed the meeting schedule for 2020. The GPAC agreed that the due to Holidays in
January and February, there will be a meeting on January 30th at 6:00pm and the February meeting
will be canceled. Thereafter, the meetings will be held on the third Tuesday of every month at 6:00
pm.
7.  ADJOURNMENT
CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 8:35 pm. The next General Plan Advisory Committee
meeting will be held on Thursday, January 30, 2020 at 6:00 pm in the City of Rolling Hills Estates
Council Chamber.
